article_title: What differentiates educational literature? A multimodal fusion approach of transformers and computational linguistics
citation: Jordan J. Bird. (2024). What Differentiates Educational Literature? A Multimodal Fusion Approach of Transformers and Computational Linguistics. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.17593
title: Publicly released UK Key Stage readability dataset of 20,000 balanced text chunks
description: A dataset built from 384 Project Gutenberg books cross-referenced with Lexile scores, segmented into chunks of up to 512 tokens and balanced to 5,000 rows per Key Stage. The article states it "resulted in a full dataset size of 20,000 data objects, with 5,000 belonging to each Key Stage 2, 3, 4, and 5", split 80/20 for training and validation, and released publicly under the MIT license on Kaggle for interdisciplinary reuse.
requirements: Books require an available Lexile score to be retained; Key Stage 1 texts were unavailable and excluded
constraints: The study undersampled the full corpus due to computational resource limits, as the authors state
target_learners: UK Key Stage 2–5 secondary and post-16 English students
target_learning_goals: Matching English literature texts to appropriate educational stages and reading difficulty
examples: Lowest Lexile score in the dataset was 420 (The Monkey's Paw); highest was 1840 (Discourse on the Method)
key_sources: Jordan J. Bird. (2024). What Differentiates Educational Literature? A Multimodal Fusion Approach of Transformers and Computational Linguistics. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.17593

article_title: Students as Radical Agents of Change
citation: Fielding, M. (2001). Students as Radical Agents of Change. Journal of Educational Change, 2, 123–141. https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1017949213447
title: UK high school Students as Researchers partnership running since 1996
description: A long-running joint project in a UK high school in which students act as researchers, developed since 1996 and described as still current at the time of writing. The abstract states the paper describes "the still current joint work in a UK high school that has developed since 1996" and gives practical examples of the Students as Researchers approach in that setting.
requirements: Sustained researcher–school partnership over multiple years
examples: Practical examples from the school's project are given in the paper
key_sources: Fielding, M. (2001). Students as Radical Agents of Change. Journal of Educational Change, 2, 123–141. https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1017949213447

article_title: Performance of GPT-4o and o1-Pro on United Kingdom Medical Licensing Assessment-style items: a comparative study.
citation: Vakili B, Ahmad A, Zolfaghari M. (2025). Performance of GPT-4o and o1-Pro on United Kingdom Medical Licensing Assessment-style items: a comparative study. Journal of Educational Evaluation for Health Professions. https://doi.org/10.3352/jeehp.2025.22.30
title: Curated UKMLA-style item dataset (374 text-based and 20 image-based items from Geeky Medics)
description: The article curates a licensed dataset of UKMLA-style single-best-answer items used to benchmark two LLMs. Of "394 UKMLA-style SBA items" screened, 374 text-only items were included (Dataset 1) and "Twenty image-based items were analyzed separately (Dataset 2)", covering clinical photographs, radiological imaging, electrocardiography, and histopathology slides. Items required a single stem, 5 options, and 1 best answer.
requirements: Items screened by two resident doctors for clear SBA format and relevance to the UKMLA syllabus, with discrepancies resolved by consensus
constraints: Items came from a licensed third-party item bank (Geeky Medics), which may not fully capture the breadth, standard-setting, or item formats of the official exam
target_learners: UK medical students preparing for the UKMLA
target_learning_goals: Applied clinical knowledge across medical specialties assessed by single-best-answer items
examples: Each item was entered verbatim into each model with a standardized prompt requesting only the letter of the chosen option, in a new chat window with default parameters
key_sources: Vakili B, Ahmad A, Zolfaghari M. (2025). Performance of GPT-4o and o1-Pro on United Kingdom Medical Licensing Assessment-style items: a comparative study. Journal of Educational Evaluation for Health Professions. https://doi.org/10.3352/jeehp.2025.22.30

article_title: Big data analysis: examination of the relationship between candidates' sociodemographic characteristics and performance in the UK's Membership of the Royal College of Physicians Part 1 examination.
citation: Johnston Peter W., Vieira Rute, Cameron Isobel M., Kumwenda Ben, Walker Kim A., Cleland Jennifer A. (2025). Big data analysis: examination of the relationship between candidates' sociodemographic characteristics and performance in the UK's Membership of the Royal College of Physicians Part 1 examination. Advances in Health Sciences Education 30(1), 53-68. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10459-024-10406-3
title: UK Medical Education Database (UKMED) linked dataset enabling granular differential-attainment analysis
description: UKMED is a database "which holds educational outcomes for all medical students and postgraduate trainees in approved UK medical schools and training programmes by crosslinking data from several sources, including the Higher Education Statistics Authority (HESA) Limited and the General Medical Council (GMC)". In this study it supplied anonymised, linked sociodemographic, programme, EPM, SJT and MRCP Part 1 records for 6040 graduates, analysed within a secure Data Safe Haven. Researchers can apply for access to the same data via UKMED.
requirements: Data must be stored, handled and analysed within a safe haven in accordance with security, governance and confidentiality standards, as the article describes.
constraints: The article notes big data studies are inevitably limited by the data that are available, including incomplete EPM and SJT recording for earlier cohorts.
target_learners: UK medical students and postgraduate medical trainees
target_learning_goals: Understanding group-level patterns of performance and differential attainment across the medical education pathway
examples: The study extracted records for doctors with a UK primary medical qualification in 2012-2014 who sat MRCP Part 1 before October 2019.
key_sources: Johnston Peter W., Vieira Rute, Cameron Isobel M., Kumwenda Ben, Walker Kim A., Cleland Jennifer A. (2025).
